## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A thirty-*juǎn* compilation of the ritual handbooks of the *Yùtáng dàfǎ* 玉堂大法 ("Great Method of the Jade Hall") tradition founded by [路時中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B7%AF%E6%99%82%E4%B8%AD). As the text explains, the *Yùtáng* 玉堂 is formed out of the *qì* of Mount Yùjīng 玉京 and houses the *Jiǔlǎo* 九老, the Nine Ancients (1.2b). The main body falls into three blocks corresponding to the school's three degrees of initiation: the "Unsurpassed Doctrine in Twenty-Four Sections" (*wúshàng zōngzhǐ èrshísì pǐn* 無上宗旨二十四品, *j.* 1–23), corresponding to the highest degree (cf. 2.6a, 26.1b–2a, 28.7a–b); the funeral liturgy of the *Língbǎo dàfǎ* 靈寶大法 type (*j.* 14–18); and the "Seven Sections for the Initial Degree" (*chūjiē qīpǐn* 初階七品, *j.* 26–28). The work contains [路時中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B7%AF%E6%99%82%E4%B8%AD)'s own colophon at 1.7a–8a, and a second colophon at the end of *j.* 28 narrating the school's revelations of 1107–1158. The *Yùtáng dàfǎ* is defined here as the *nèibì* 內祕 (inner secret) of the *Tiānxīn zhèngfǎ* 天心正法 (26.1a) and as the essential method of Zhāng Dàolíng — "the fundamental oath between *Xuányuán* (Tàishàng lǎojūn) and the Sagely Master" (1.7b). Its three foundational *fú* — the *Sānguāng zǔfú* 三光祖符, the *Hēishā fú* 黑煞符, and the *Tiāngāng fú* 天罡符 — are the same three *fú* that anchor the *Tiānxīn zhèngfǎ* (cf. *[DZ 1227 Tàishàng zhùguó jiùmín zǒngzhēn bìyào](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c1227)* 2.10a–17a; *[DZ 566 Shàngqīng tiānxīn zhèngfǎ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0566)* 3.1a–9a).

**Abstract**

Poul Andersen, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:1070–1074 (§3.B.5, Tiānxīn Zhèngfǎ and Related Rites), establishes that the work is at once the founding manual of the *Yùtáng dàfǎ* and the key witness for its self-understanding as the inner-meditative core of the *Tiānxīn zhèngfǎ*. Zhái Rǔwén (*zì* Gōngxùn 公巽, 1076–1141) — co-recipient of the 1107 revelations — was a noted scholar-official, calligrapher, and painter (cf. *Sòngshǐ* 372.11543–45 and the epitaph in his *Zhōnghuì jí* 忠惠集). He compiled a *Méngzhēn yùjiàn* 盟真玉鑑 in ten *juǎn* and a *Jīnggōng pǔjì yí* 景宮普濟儀 in three *juǎn* for the *Míngyáng zhāi* 明陽齋, both ritual compendia in a style comparable to the present work. Jīn Yǔnzhōng 金允中 in *[DZ 1223 Shàngqīng língbǎo dàfǎ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c1223)* 41.17a–b describes the present text as a revised version, edited by [路時中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B7%AF%E6%99%82%E4%B8%AD) in the early Shàoxīng period (1131–1162), of the earlier compilation by Yuán Miàozōng 元妙宗 — i.e., *[DZ 1227 Tàishàng zhùguó jiùmín zǒngzhēn bìyào](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c1227)* (dated 1116). The school's exposition of progressive initiation (2.6a, 26.1b–2a) requires the novice to first receive a ten-*juǎn* *Tiānxīn zhèngfǎ* and practice it for three years before ascending to the initial degree of the *Yùtáng dàfǎ*; only the *běntán* 本壇 edition of *Tiānxīn zhèngfǎ* is permitted (26.1b). The funeral rites of *j.* 14–18, by contrast, are *Língbǎo dàfǎ* in form: *[DZ 466 Língbǎo lǐngjiào jìdù jīnshū](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0466)* 260.1a reports that [路時中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B7%AF%E6%99%82%E4%B8%AD) transmitted the *Língbǎo dàfǎ* in Jiànkāng 建康 during the Zhènghé period (1111–1117). Frontmatter dates 1107–1158 to bracket the revelation-and-redaction period.
